title: Q-ASHBY-markov: read the work queue as a Markov chain and find the states items cannot leave
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe markov-chain
**Status:** closed

Problem: The kernel keeps each item's current status and not its transitions, so it cannot say which states absorb items or how long closure takes. Ashby's journal (index: Markov process, J.4539 to J.4545, J.4700; ultrastability in Markov machines, J.4904; Absorbing state; self-locking states collect every member of an ensemble, J.4055, J.4229) treats progress to an absorbing state as the stochastic form of stability.

Build: Add a migration with table `item_transitions (item_id, from_status, to_status, at)` written where `seed/worker/src/tick.js` changes an item's status, and `export function absorption(transitions, allowed)` to `seed/worker/src/ashby.js`: the transition matrix, its absorbing states and closed classes, those not in `allowed` (done, superseded, cancelled), and the expected steps to absorption from each state. Builtin metric `items_trapped` (items in a closed class outside the allowed set, target 0) with a goal under `core.adapt` in `seed/autonomy/goals.json`. Tests in `seed/worker/test/ashby.test.js` on a chain with a known fundamental matrix. Bind the concept `markov-chain` in `doctrine/ashby-concepts.json`.

**Prediction:** ashby_gaps <= 3 within 720 h

**Out of scope:** predicting single items; rows older than the retention window in `seed/autonomy/retention.json`.

size: M

**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe markov-chain` passes when the concept is implemented and every mechanism it names exists (ASHBY-KERNEL-1).

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-27T10:02:06Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 6.1 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
